question: Did Portuguese pressure on Muslim coastal commerce help reorient some Muslim communities toward the Kandyan interior and eastern routes?
mechanism: Loss or restriction of access to selected Portuguese-dominated coastal nodes increased the value of alternative political protection and inland/eastern commercial corridors; Kandyan rulers in turn could benefit from merchants and specialists with transregional contacts.
transmission_channel: coastal commercial pressure -> spatial relocation/reorientation -> Kandyan protection and intermediary functions
time_lag: sixteenth to seventeenth centuries, with longer-term eastern/inland settlement consequences
scale: Z1 coastal settlements to Z3 kingdom/regional networks
bounded_by: Do not infer that all Muslim settlement in Kandy or the east resulted from Portuguese expulsions; several migration and settlement processes overlapped.
